question: Should OpenClaw add a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ-style orchestration as external only, or defer the broad worker-queue layer until narrower HA/runtime trackers settle?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the backend boundary, config shape, worker claiming semantics, credential model, observability surface, and core-versus-plugin ownership are product and architecture decisions automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and security review requirements before any Redis/BullMQ-specific implementation lands.

options.title: Document External Orchestration
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern without adding core runtime surfaces.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and worker-auth issues establish core boundaries first, then revisit whether a broad distributed worker layer is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and security review requirements before any Redis/BullMQ-specific implementation lands.
